# layout.focus-visible — Keyboard focus reaches an element that shows no visible indicator

- **Check ID:** `layout.focus-visible`
- **Default severity:** `error`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`, `browser` (only with `--rendered`)
- **Standards:** WCAG 2.4.7
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/focus-visible.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/layout.focus-visible.md`](../layout.focus-visible.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

An element the keyboard can reach takes focus and nothing about how it looks changes — no ring, no colour, no shadow, no shape shift.

## Why it matters

A keyboard user moves by pressing Tab and finds their place by looking for the highlight. When a link or button suppresses its focus outline and nothing replaces it, the highlight simply is not there, and the whole page becomes unreachable without a mouse: the user keeps tabbing past the control they were aiming for. This is a hard failure of WCAG 2.4.7, one of a handful of success criteria every site has to meet, and it is common on pages where an author wrote `a:focus { outline: none }` and stopped there.

## What it checks

In a real browser, the check presses Tab through the page one stop at a time. Before it starts, it captures the computed appearance of every element on the page and of each of their `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements; at each stop, it captures that appearance again and compares.

An element fails when nothing a focus change could repaint now looks different from before anything had focus: not the element itself, not any ancestor (a common pattern is a card that lights up on `:focus-within`), not a sibling, not a descendant, and none of the same elements' pseudo-elements. What the author used does not matter — outline, box-shadow, background, border, text colour, weight, underline, opacity, transform, size, `content`: any change is a pass. That is why `outline: none` with a replacement — the pattern WCAG itself recommends — is never reported here.

Only visible outlines count. An outline with no style, zero width, or a fully transparent colour is recorded as no outline at all, so `a:focus { outline: 3px solid transparent }` does not masquerade as an indicator. `outline-offset` is not compared, because Chromium moves it on focus even when the ring itself is suppressed and the pair would then never differ.

Every page is measured at three widths — phone (375 px), tablet (768 px), and desktop (1280 px) — because an indicator can exist at one width and not at another. One element stays one finding however many widths it was seen at, and the finding names those widths (`Seen at phone (375 px), tablet (768 px), desktop (1280 px).`).

The check needs a browser and is opt-in: it runs only under `--rendered` or `enable.browser` (see [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-headless-browser.md)). Pages load from `file://` URLs, remote requests are refused during the run, and the browser is the machine's own — it is never downloaded. There is no broken fixture for it in the fixture gate for the same reason.

**Assumption.** The judgement follows the host browser's own default focus ring, so this check assumes a Chromium browser: an unstyled link passes because Chromium's UA sheet paints a `:focus-visible` outline and the check reads that outline. Other engines paint something different; a run on a machine with only a WebKit or Gecko browser is still consistent, but the exact "default look" being compared is different.

**Shapes it refuses to guess.** An indicator a measurement cannot see is not evidence of its absence, so these are skipped rather than reported:

- **Shadow DOM and custom elements.** Anything whose tag contains a hyphen, or whose element hosts a shadow root, paints from inside a tree the main document's computed styles do not reach.
- **Elements only a script focuses.** A negative `tabindex` means Tab never lands there for a person, so the ring shown by a script-driven `.focus()` is not what a keyboard user sees.
- **Content hidden from assistive tech.** Elements inside `aria-hidden="true"` or `inert` are `a11y.hidden-focusable`'s finding: one problem, one finding.
- **Self-animating elements.** An element on an infinite CSS animation repaints whatever focus does, so its appearance carries no information. Transitions are not infinite and stay in scope: an indicator that fades in on focus is one a person sees.
- **Pages that load CSS from a CDN.** The run is offline, remote requests are refused, so what the browser would have measured is not what a person sees. When any stylesheet — a `<link>` or an `@import` — has a `http(s)` source, the whole page is skipped.

One limit follows from the method rather than from a choice: an indicator painted inside a control's own UA shadow tree — the `<video>` and `<audio>` transport bars — is not readable from the main document's computed styles. Those elements are judged only on what their own computed style does when focus arrives; in Chromium that changes, so they pass, but the check is not measuring their ring.

## How to fix

Give the element a focus indicator that is clearly visible against the page. Style `:focus-visible` rather than `:focus` so the ring appears for keyboard users and stays hidden for mouse clicks. Keep any `outline: none` paired with its replacement in the same rule, so the removal cannot outlive the substitution.

```css
/* before: the ring is gone and nothing replaces it */
a:focus { outline: none; }

/* after: a ring on keyboard focus, no ring on mouse focus */
a:focus { outline: none; }
a:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid currentColor;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

Some pages light the wrapping card on focus rather than the control itself. That is an indicator and this check accepts it, but keep the pairing together so removing one does not leave the other orphaned:

```css
/* a card whose focus ring lives on the wrapper */
.card:focus-within { outline: 2px solid #005fcc; outline-offset: 3px; }
.card a:focus { outline: none; }
```

There is no automatic edit: the fix lives in the page's source stylesheet, not in the built HTML the finding points at, and which technique to use depends on what the surrounding design can carry.

None.
